results.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
results.proof_sketch: An induced-minor model gives these sets as the inverse images of the six target vertices under contractions. The absent target edge forces A and B to be anticomplete, since edge deletion is unavailable. Conversely, contract each connected set; all fourteen required edges appear and the A-B edge does not. For the algorithm, assign every vertex one of seven labels: unused or one of the six branch sets. For each assignment, test nonemptiness, connectivity, the forbidden A-B adjacency, and the fourteen required adjacencies. The labels themselves are a polynomial-size NP certificate.

results.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
results.proof_sketch: If q=0, G is complete and cannot contain two anticomplete nonempty branch sets. If q>0 and G has at least four universal vertices, the endpoints of any nonedge together with four universal vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices. Every remaining vertex is an endpoint of a nonedge, so there are at most 2q such vertices and n≤2q+3. Apply the seven-label algorithm from the first claim. This also gives a kernel: output a fixed yes/no instance in the two decided cases and retain G otherwise.

results.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
results.proof_sketch: Take a branch model and restrict G to its six branch sets. Each Ci supplies an A-B path whose internal vertices lie in Ci, so every separator disjoint from A∪B has size at least four. Choose an inclusion-minimal A-B separator S. Minimality makes each s∈S adjacent into both components DA and DB containing A and B. If two vertices of S were nonadjacent, shortest paths between them through DA and DB would form an induced cycle of length at least four; hence S is a clique. Each full component D contains a vertex complete to S: choose v∈D maximizing |N(v)∩S|. If s∈S misses v, take a shortest path v=p0,…,pk in D to a neighbor pk of s. For every t∈N(v)∩S, applying chordality to the cycle through t,p0,…,pk,s (using the last neighbor of t on the path) forces tpk to be an edge. Then pk has strictly more neighbors in S than v, a contradiction. Select S-complete vertices x∈DA and y∈DB and four vertices of S. Since x and y lie in different components, these six vertices induce precisely K6 minus xy.

results.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
results.proof_sketch: The two anticomplete exceptional branch sets must lie in one part: fixing a vertex in either set forces every vertex of the other set, and then of both sets, into that same part. Since a part is independent and each branch set is connected, both are singletons. A core branch touching them is either a singleton in another part or spans at least two parts. Any spanning branch can be shrunk to one cross-part edge; such an edge is adjacent to every other spanning branch and to every outside-part singleton. Singleton core branches must occupy distinct outside parts. Thus choose their part set J, and the remaining core branches are exactly disjoint cross-part edges, namely a matching. The displayed matching formula follows by pairing vertices from different parts: at most ⌊M/2⌋ edges are possible, and every edge uses a vertex outside a largest part, giving M−L; greedily pairing different largest remaining parts attains the minimum. Enumerating i,s,J costs O(r^5), after finding the parts as complement components.

results.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
results.proof_sketch: Use a nice tree decomposition. A state assigns each bag vertex one of the six branch labels or unused; records, for every label, the partition of its bag vertices into connected components already built; records whether that label is unseen, active, or completed; and stores fourteen bits for required inter-branch adjacencies. Processing an edge merges same-label components, sets the appropriate adjacency bit, or rejects an A-B edge. When the last bag vertex of a component is forgotten, separator locality implies that component cannot connect later, so it may disappear only as the unique component of its label, after which that label is closed. Join nodes combine compatible assignments and partitions by transitive closure and union their adjacency bits; they reject two completed off-bag copies of one label. At the empty root require all six labels completed and all fourteen bits set. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a pattern-dependent constant states, which is 2^{O(w log w)}.

results.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
results.proof_sketch: The two paths and the four singleton sets {ci} form a valid model. Suppose instead that an exceptional branch is {x}. Its four core neighbors require four distinct neighbors of x. Path vertices have degree at most three, so x=ci. The other exceptional branch Y is a connected interval in one component of A−ai or B−bi. Its four core neighbors require |N(Y)\Y|≥4. Up to swapping A,B and reversing indices, take x=c1 or c2. For c2, every allowable interval has at most three external neighbors. For c1, the only intervals with four external neighbors are {a2,a3} and {a2,a3,a4}. Their respective external neighborhoods are {a1,a4,c2,c3} and {a1,c2,c3,c4}. Four disjoint core branches must therefore use all four boundary vertices, including a1. But a1 is isolated after deleting x and Y, so its core branch is the singleton {a1}, anticomplete to the other three core branches—a contradiction. Symmetry handles all remaining cases.

results.claim: In every subcubic graph, each exceptional branch set in a K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor model has at least two vertices and each of the four core branch sets has at least three vertices. Consequently every such model uses at least 16 vertices.
results.proof_sketch: Let S be a connected k-vertex branch set and let δ(S) be its edge boundary. Since G[S] has at least k−1 edges and every vertex has degree at most three, |δ(S)|=∑_{v∈S}deg(v)−2|E(G[S])|≤3k−2(k−1)=k+2. An exceptional branch must have an edge to each of four pairwise-disjoint core branches, so |δ(S)|≥4 and k≥2. A core branch must have an edge to each of the other five branch sets, so |δ(S)|≥5 and k≥3. Summing the six lower bounds gives 2+2+4·3=16.

results.claim: The subcubic lower bound is tight: the following 16-vertex cubic graph contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor. Its six branch paths are A=a1a2, B=b1b2, and Ci=ci1ci2ci3 for i=1,…,4. Besides the path edges, add a1c11,a1c21,a2c31,a2c41, b1c11,b1c21,b2c31,b2c41, c12c22,c32c42,c13c33,c13c43,c23c33,c23c43, and no other edges.
results.proof_sketch: Every a- or b-vertex has its path edge and two listed core neighbors. Each ci1 has one path edge plus its listed A- and B-neighbors; each ci2 has two path edges plus c12c22 or c32c42; each ci3 has one path edge plus two of the four listed cross edges. Thus every vertex has degree three. A and B are anticomplete. The eight A/B-to-core edges supply their eight required branch adjacencies, and the final six edges supply exactly one adjacency for every pair of core paths. Hence the six paths form a valid model. The preceding bound shows that every model in this graph uses at least 16 vertices and has no singleton branch set.

results.claim: For ℓ≥1, let Xℓ be obtained by replacing every edge of the preceding 16-vertex cubic graph by a path of ℓ edges. Then Xℓ is connected and bridgeless, has 24ℓ−8 vertices, 24ℓ edges, maximum degree 3, cycle rank 9, and treewidth exactly 4, and contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor.
results.proof_sketch: The base graph has 16 vertices and 24 edges, so uniform ℓ-subdivision gives 16+24(ℓ−1)=24ℓ−8 vertices and 24ℓ edges; its cycle rank is therefore 24ℓ−(24ℓ−8)+1=9. Contracting every subdivision path restores the audited base graph and its target model. Every base edge lies on a cycle. For a cross-branch edge, lift a target cycle containing its corresponding edge. For an internal branch-path edge, both resulting sides contain external attachments, and the target with that branch vertex removed is connected, so an outside route closes a cycle through the internal edge. Subdivision preserves bridgelessness, and all degrees are two or three. For the base graph, the filled elimination order a1,b1,c12,c23,c13,c22,c32,c43,c33,a2,b2,c11,c21,c31,c41,c42 has later-degree sequence 3,3,3,3,4,4,3,4,4,4,4,4,3,2,1,0. Eliminating subdivision vertices along each path first restores this width-4 order. The target is an ordinary minor and has treewidth 4, so minor-monotonicity gives equality.

results.claim: Every K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor model in Xℓ is spanning. Consequently its largest branch set has at least 4ℓ−1 vertices. Thus branch-set size is unbounded even for subcubic hosts of the minimum possible maximum degree and treewidth.
results.proof_sketch: The binary cycle-space dimension of a graph is its cycle rank. Let U be the union of a model's six branch sets. The target has cycle rank 14−6+1=9, and contractions and simplification cannot increase cycle rank, so Xℓ[U] has cycle rank at least 9. If U were proper, choose v outside U. Because Xℓ is bridgeless, v lies on a cycle. The cycle space of Xℓ[U] embeds into the 9-dimensional cycle space of Xℓ but does not contain that cycle, which uses an edge incident with v. It is therefore a proper subspace and has dimension at most 8, a contradiction. Hence U=V(Xℓ). The six disjoint branch sets partition 24ℓ−8 vertices, so one has size at least ⌈(24ℓ−8)/6⌉=4ℓ−1. In a maximum-degree-2 graph the boundary identity gives |δ(S)|≤2 for every connected S, too few for an exceptional branch's four core adjacencies. Treewidth below 4 is impossible because the target is an ordinary minor. Thus both restrictions on Xℓ are sharp.

results.claim: For every integer ℓ≥1, let Fℓ consist of a clique Q={c0,c1,c2,c3}, two mutually anticomplete induced paths a0…a(3ℓ) and b0…b(3ℓ), and, besides the clique and path edges, exactly the edges ci-a(iℓ) and ci-b(iℓ) for i=0,1,2,3. Then Fℓ has maximum degree 5 and treewidth exactly 4, and it contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor.
results.proof_sketch: The two full paths and the four singleton sets {ci} are a model, so Fℓ contains the target. Every ci has its three clique neighbors and two path neighbors, while every path vertex has degree at most three; hence the maximum degree is 5. For the upper treewidth bound, use filled elimination order a0,…,a(3ℓ), b0,…,b(3ℓ), c0,c1,c2,c3. When aj is eliminated, its later neighbors are a(j+1), if present, together with c0,…,c⌊j/ℓ⌋; fill from earlier eliminations creates exactly these propagated clique neighbors. There are at most four, and the same holds on the b-path; the remaining Q is a four-clique. Thus tw(Fℓ)≤4. Conversely, the displayed model is also an ordinary K6-minus-an-edge minor. That target has treewidth 4: it contains a K5, and eliminating one endpoint of its missing edge leaves a K5. Minor-monotonicity gives tw(Fℓ)≥4.

results.claim: In Fℓ, the minimum, over all K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor models, of max(|A|,|B|) for the two exceptional nonadjacent branch sets is exactly ℓ+1. Consequently no constant depending only on the target can bound both exceptional branch sets, even on hosts of maximum degree 5 and the minimum possible treewidth 4.
results.proof_sketch: For the lower bound, the two exceptional branches cannot both meet Q, because Q is a clique and they are anticomplete. Choose one, S, that avoids Q. Since Fℓ−Q is the disjoint union of the two paths, connected S is an interval in one path. If it contains r attachment sites, its edge boundary has at most r+2 edges: r edges to Q and at most two path edges. It must touch four disjoint core branches, so it has at least four distinct boundary edges. Hence r≥2, and attachment sites are ℓ edges apart, giving |S|≥ℓ+1. Thus max(|A|,|B|)≥ℓ+1 in every model. Equality is attained by taking A={aj:ℓ≤j≤2ℓ} and B={bj:ℓ≤j≤2ℓ}; take D1={c1}, D2={c2}, D0={c0}∪{aj,bj:0≤j<ℓ}, and D3={c3}∪{aj,bj:2ℓ<j≤3ℓ}. The six sets are connected and disjoint; A,B are anticomplete; the four D-sets are pairwise adjacent through Q; and each D-set touches both intervals at the corresponding attachment or path-boundary edge.

final_writeup:
The unrestricted P-versus-NP-complete classification is not resolved here. The eight independently verified parent results are retained: an exact branch-set certificate gives NP membership and an exponential algorithm; the number of nonedges yields an FPT kernel; chordal inputs reduce to induced-subgraph detection; complete multipartite inputs have an explicit count-and-matching criterion; supplied bounded-width decompositions support a connectivity dynamic program; singleton normalization fails; and the sharp subcubic model-size threshold is 16.

The mandated lens gives two unbounded normalization obstructions at sharp host boundaries. First, uniformly ℓ-subdivide every edge of the parent’s tight cubic graph. The resulting Xℓ is subcubic, has treewidth 4, and is bridgeless with cycle rank 9, exactly that of K6 minus an edge. Deleting any vertex strictly lowers its cycle-space dimension, while taking an induced minor cannot increase that dimension. Hence every target model in Xℓ is spanning. Its six branches partition 24ℓ−8 vertices, so its largest branch has at least 4ℓ−1 vertices. Maximum degree 3 and treewidth 4 are both the least possible for a host.

Second, spacing the four attachment sites in the parent’s 12-vertex example gives an exception-specific bound. Form Fℓ from two anticomplete paths with attachment sites 0,ℓ,2ℓ,3ℓ and a four-clique whose ith vertex attaches to the ith site on both paths. In every model at least one exceptional branch avoids the clique and is a path interval. Four distinct core adjacencies require four boundary edges; only two can leave through the path, so the interval contains two ℓ-spaced attachment sites and has at least ℓ+1 vertices. This is exact: choose both middle intervals as the exceptional branches and combine the two prefixes and two suffixes with the outer clique vertices as cores. Thus no target-dependent constant can bound all branches—or even both exceptional branches—on bounded-degree, treewidth-4 hosts.

These obstructions rule out bounded-branch guessing as a general route, but supply neither an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm nor an NP-hardness reduction. The source target’s unrestricted classification remains open in this draft, so the resolution is PARTIAL.
